_doc: Training data recipe — 'Broad Brain' mix v2.
Goal: train a SMALL model (50M-350M params) to be genuinely useful at
code, math, reasoning, real-world problem solving, AND blockchain/web3 —
while keeping the persona on top via --corpus and --distill-corpus weights.
Honest framing: at 50M (small) or 280M (home-11gb) params trained on
~30M total tokens, this model will NOT match Claude Code / Codex. The
compute gap is multiple orders of magnitude (Claude Opus = trillions of
params × trillions of tokens × thousands of GPU-years; this is the
absolute opposite end of the scale spectrum). What it WILL do well:
simple Python / TypeScript / Solidity, algebra + math word problems,
multi-step reasoning, conversation in your voice, basic instruction
following. Treat it as a thoughtful small assistant, not a frontier LM.
How to use locally:
bash scripts/train/run-home-max.sh \
--resume \
--variant home-11gb \
--batch 2 --grad-accum 4 --no-compile \
--mix-config scripts/data/mix-broadbrain.json
GitHub Actions uses this recipe by default in .github/workflows/pretrain.yml
Trade-off note on data sources:
Several entries (MetaMathQA, UltraChat, Magicoder-Evol, MathInstruct,
UltraInteract) are SYNTHETIC — generated by larger LLMs as instruction
data. Training small models on them is the standard 'distillation'
recipe (Phi-3, DeepSeek, every modern <1B model uses it). If you want
ZERO synthetic data, remove those entries — you'll lose ~60% of
capability coverage but the model will only learn from human-written
text. The defaults below keep them in for capability density.
Coverage matrix:
• Persona voice:           distill-corpus + base-corpus
• Narrative warmup:        TinyStories
• Human-written quality:   dolly + no_robots
• Code (Python):           the-stack-python + code-alpaca + magicoder
• Code (TypeScript/JS):    the-stack-typescript
• Code (Solidity / web3):  the-stack-solidity
• Math:                    MetaMathQA + MathInstruct
• Reasoning / STEM:        Open-Platypus + UltraInteract
• Multi-turn chat:         UltraChat-200k

sources.name: tinystories
sources.note: Narrative warmup. Tiny clean English — helps embeddings stabilise.

sources.name: no-robots
sources.note: 10K examples human-curated by skilled annotators — ZERO synthetic. Best instruction-following quality per token in the entire mix.

sources.name: the-stack-python
sources.note: Real Python from public GitHub. Pure code, no instructions.

sources.name: the-stack-typescript
sources.note: TypeScript from public GitHub. Crucial for Next.js / React / web dev — the user's stack.

sources.name: the-stack-solidity
sources.note: Solidity smart contracts from public GitHub. Web3 / blockchain coverage. Less data than Python because the language is smaller in the wild.

sources.name: code-alpaca
sources.note: Code instructions ('write a function that…') in alpaca format. 20k examples.

sources.name: magicoder-evol
sources.note: 110K evolved code instructions — the highest-quality code SFT dataset on HF. Heavy uplift on the 'real-world problem solving' axis.

sources.name: metamath
sources.note: 395K math word problems with worked chain-of-thought solutions.

sources.name: mathinstruct
sources.note: Hybrid CoT + program-of-thought (PoT) math instructions. Strong on word problems AND symbolic algebra. Synthetic.

sources.name: open-platypus
sources.note: STEM reasoning, logic, science. Curated from many sources.

sources.name: ultrainteract
sources.note: Tree-structured CoT reasoning from openbmb. Strongest 'real-world problem solving' signal in the mix.
